previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 52-year-old female with systemic lupus erythematosus and end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis was admitted with a severe posterior headache, neck stiffness, and low-grade fever. Initial evaluation included a normal head CT and lumbar puncture showing no signs of infection. She had new subcutaneous nodules on her left leg, concerning for septic emboli, prompting dermatology consultation and biopsy, which showed only extravasated red blood cells. Blood cultures were negative, and echocardiogram showed no new vegetation, though a calcified mitral valve area could not be fully ruled out. Liver enzymes were acutely elevated but improved rapidly, with hepatology attributing this to a likely passed biliary stone. The fever resolved without a definitive source, and the headache subsided after admission. She was treated with IV antibiotics initially but was transitioned to oral care as her condition stabilized. She was discharged home afebrile with instructions to follow up on pending labs, dental care, and outpatient appointments.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is a ___ with h/o SLE, ESRD ___ to lupus 
nephritis, CMP (EF 60-65%), who presents with shortness of 
breath, concerning for fluid overload. 

# Shortness of breath: Patient with acute onset shortness of 
breath, likely secondary to flash pulmonary edema. Other 
considerations include pneumonia (bibasilar infiltrate on 
initial CXR and cough x1 week), versus worsening of mitral 
regurgitation. She has a h/o cardiomyopathy, most recent EF 
60-65% on ECHO in ___. Patient underwent dialysis for 2.3 
liters fluid removal on the first hospital day and her 
oxygenation improved such that she was weaned to 2 liters by 
nasal cannula. She had a repeat CXR that showed decreased 
bilateral opacifications consistent with some improvement in 
pulmonary vascular congestion in addition more focal area of 
opacification especially in the retrocardiac region that could 
represent superimposed pneumonia especially since there has been 
obscuration of the left hemidiaphragm. In addition, she 
underwent echocardiogram on the second hospital day that showed 
similar findings compared to her prior (___). On discharge, 
she felt that her breathing was at baseline and had no oxygen 
requirement. Overall, it is likely she had flash pulmonary edema 
from fluid overload. 

# Possible Pneumonia

left hemidiaphragm and cough, the patient was treated for 
community-acquired pneumonia with ciprofloxacin for a 7 day 
course (End date: ___. HAC is a consideration given she is a 
dialysis patient, so she will have close outpatient follow-up.

calcium.

drip. However, after hemodialysis her blood pressures came down, 
nitro gtt was stopped, and she was transitioned to her home

normotensive on discharge.
